./cluster --nodes 3

~/dist/cluster simulated

Three nodes run a small Raft-style cluster, or an AP store, inside your browser. Nothing here touches a network: it is a toy with a fake clock, built to show what the chapters describe. Try the experiments below the controls.

=

# event log





# experiments


    

  1. Crash the leader. In CP mode, press kill on the leader. Watch a follower time out, raise its term and win with 2 of 3 votes. Revive the old leader: it comes back as a follower.
    2. 

  2. Lose the majority. Kill two nodes, then write to the survivor. It cannot commit (1 of 3), so the entry stays dashed. This is the cluster choosing consistency over availability. Revive one node and the write commits.
    3. 

  3. Split brain, avoided. Press isolate on the leader, then write to it. The other two elect a new leader and take writes. Heal: the old leader's uncommitted entry is discarded. This is the same story as the consensus lab.
    4. 

  4. Stale read. In AP mode isolate n3, write x=1 to n1, then read x from n3. It answers (available) with an old or missing value (not consistent).
    5. 

  5. Last write wins. In AP mode isolate n3 and write x=A on n1 and x=B on n3, then heal. One value survives and the other write is silently lost. Compare with the replication lab.
    6. 



Simplifications: ticks instead of milliseconds, no disk, no cluster changes, a global clock for last-write-wins (real clocks drift, which makes LWW worse). The Raft rules for terms, votes, log matching and majority commit are followed. Read the real thing: raft.github.io.
